title: Combinators on the Battlefield: BCKW and SKI Reduction in Magic: The Gathering
description:
Terms of combinatory logic (BCKW and SKI) are encoded directly as game objects in Magic: The Gathering: a term is a forest of Aura permanents with "Enchant permanent", and application is attachment. Three game actions, each the printed effect of a real paper card, reduce such a forest in normal order: re-attach an Aura, copy one Aura as a token, and sacrifice an Aura, after which state-based actions delete K's discarded argument.

The model is cooperative, not forced: one player chooses every action. This is not a claim that Magic is Turing complete in the forced sense of Churchill, Biderman and Herrick. A Python model of the moves agrees step for step with a reference normal-order reducer on the terms tested; it models the moves and selected rule mechanics, not the rules of Magic. Rules legality rests on a reading of the Comprehensive Rules of 6 November 2026, with no judge confirmation.

The deposit contains the paper, its LaTeX source, the simulators with their saved outputs, and the working notes.
